@graph.headline: Agent Family Architecture vs Agent Swarms
@graph.description: Designing collaborative agent families: specialized subagent roles, team council governance, and clean handoff protocols.
@graph.keywords: agent family architecture, subagent patterns, multi-agent council, hierarchical agent systems, agent coordination
@graph.abstract: Monolithic AI agents stumble when forced to juggle research, writing, styling, and code validation simultaneously. The Agent Family pattern resolves cognitive overload by delegating tasks across specialized subagents governed by a lead orchestrator, ensuring every subsystem operates within focused context limits with well-defined interface contracts.

acceptedAnswer.text: A structured collection of specialized agents that collaborate under a shared orchestrator to complete multifaceted business goals.

mainEntity.name: How do agents communicate within a family?

acceptedAnswer.text: Through structured JSON messages, shared state files, and unambiguous handoff schemas specifying requirements and success criteria.

mainEntity.name: What happens when subagents produce conflicting recommendations?

acceptedAnswer.text: A designated Council Leader or arbitration protocol evaluates arguments against defined priority weights to resolve impasses.

mainEntity.name: How do you prevent infinite loops between chatting agents?

acceptedAnswer.text: By enforcing strict recursion depth limits, task turn caps, and automated timeout watchdogs across all inter-agent dialogues.

mainEntity.name: Can subagents use different LLM models?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Specialized agents can utilize models matched to their specific task, such as fast lightweight models for routing and frontier models for synthesis.
